source_meta.issue links: Cloners:inward:MC-241277:Server can't generate amplified/large biomes worlds from scratch
source_meta._title: Server doesn't generate amplified / large biome worlds

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition using the unmodified vanilla dedicated server JAR for 1.16 Pre-release 1 and a matching 1.16 Pre-release 1 client. Run the server in a new, isolated directory on the same computer as the client so it can be reached through localhost. Use a Java runtime compatible with this historical version, with no mods, plugins, custom datapacks, or pre-existing world save.
preconditions: Obtain the exact vanilla dedicated server JAR for Minecraft Java Edition 1.16 Pre-release 1; do not substitute 1.16 Pre-release 6 or another later version.
Install or configure a Minecraft Java Edition client installation for the matching 1.16 Pre-release 1 version.
Install a Java runtime capable of launching the 1.16 Pre-release 1 server JAR.
Use a new test directory that does not contain a world folder or files from another server.
Review and accept the Minecraft EULA before setting eula=true.
Ensure the default Minecraft server port is available locally, or consistently use another configured port when connecting.
Do not copy a singleplayer world or an older server world into the test directory; the dedicated server must create the test world from scratch.

steps.action: Create a new, otherwise empty directory for this reproduction. Place the vanilla 1.16 Pre-release 1 dedicated server JAR in it and rename the file to server.jar for the commands below. Do not use a Bukkit, Spigot, Forge, Fabric, or otherwise modified server.
steps.success_cue: The isolated directory contains server.jar and no world save directory.

steps.action: Open a terminal or command prompt with its working directory set to the directory containing server.jar. Start the server once so that it can create its initial configuration files.
steps.success_cue: The server reports that the EULA must be accepted and then terminates without reaching the normal server-ready state.

steps.action: Confirm that eula.txt now exists. Open it in a plain-text editor, review the referenced EULA, change the EULA setting to true, save the file, and close the editor.
steps.success_cue: The saved eula.txt file contains eula=true.

steps.action: Open server.properties in a plain-text editor. If the file was not created during the initial launch, create a plain-text file with that exact filename in the server directory. Find the level-type property or add it if absent, and set its value exactly to the lowercase value supplied by the report. Remove any duplicate level-type entries, then save and close the file.
steps.success_cue: server.properties contains exactly one active level-type line, and that line reads level-type=amplified.

steps.action: While the server is stopped, read the value of level-name in server.properties. If the property is absent, treat its value as world. Confirm that no directory bearing that level name exists in the server directory. Because this is an isolated test directory, move or delete such a directory if one was accidentally generated; do not reuse it.
steps.success_cue: There is no existing save directory corresponding to the configured level-name, so the next launch must create the world from scratch.

steps.action: Perform a final configuration check before world creation: verify that eula.txt still contains eula=true and server.properties still contains level-type=amplified. Leave level-seed unchanged or blank because the report supplies no required seed. Do not make server.properties read-only.
steps.success_cue: The EULA is accepted, amplified is configured, and the configured level directory remains absent.

steps.action: From the terminal or command prompt whose working directory is the test server directory, launch the 1.16 Pre-release 1 server again. This launch is the trigger because the dedicated server is now asked to create a brand-new world while level-type is set to amplified.
steps.success_cue: The console identifies the running Minecraft server version as 1.16 Pre-release 1 or 1.16-pre1 and begins preparing or generating the configured level.

steps.action: Leave the server running and wait until initial spawn generation finishes. Do not connect or stop the server while the console is still reporting world preparation percentages.
steps.success_cue: The server console displays its normal Done message and accepts console input, indicating that initial world generation has completed.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition using a launcher installation explicitly configured for 1.16 Pre-release 1. If necessary, enable snapshot versions in the launcher's Installations area to expose pre-release versions; verify the version shown on the client title screen before continuing. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/minecraft-1-16-pre-release-1?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft client reaches the main menu and identifies itself as 1.16 Pre-release 1 rather than a later pre-release or release.

steps.action: From the main menu select Multiplayer, choose Direct Connect, enter localhost as the server address, and select Join Server. If the server uses a non-default port, append that same port to the address as localhost:<port>. The Direct Connect path and local-address method are standard Java Edition server connection procedures. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3AMenu_screen/Java_Edition?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The client joins the dedicated server and the player appears in the newly generated Overworld.

steps.action: Do not move far from spawn yet. Wait until the terrain surrounding the player has rendered, the loading screen has disappeared, and player looking and movement controls respond normally. Keep the server and client running at this point.
steps.success_cue: The matching client is standing in fully loaded initial chunks of the fresh world generated by the dedicated server.

stor.handoff_condition: The vanilla 1.16 Pre-release 1 dedicated server has just created a brand-new world from scratch with level-type=amplified configured, the server has reached its Done state, and a matching client is connected with the initial Overworld chunks fully rendered. Begin observation of the generated world type, terrain, and relevant world-generation metadata without regenerating or replacing the world.
uncertainties: The report supplies no world seed, coordinates, game mode, operating system, memory allocation, or Java runtime build. Leave the seed blank and otherwise retain normal server defaults unless the execution environment requires a harmless infrastructure change.

The phrase “latest pre-release” in the original steps is date-relative, but the issue metadata lists only 1.16 Pre-release 1 as affected. This plan therefore uses that exact affected version and does not use the fixed 1.16 Pre-release 6.
Comments report similar behavior for largebiomes and later pre-releases, but those versions are not present in the report's Affects versions field. They are not added to affected_versions.

This plan uses the report's primary amplified variant. To execute the separately mentioned Large Biomes variant, a separate fresh server directory and fresh world would be required with level-type=largebiomes; it should not replace or reuse this amplified test world.

The exact historical server JAR download location or checksum is not supplied. The executor must independently ensure that both the server and client identify themselves as 1.16 Pre-release 1 or 1.16-pre1 before generating the world.

Depending on the server package and first-launch behavior, server.properties might not exist after the EULA-gated launch. Step 4 therefore permits creating the file before any EULA-accepted launch can generate the test world.
